page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor configured with 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs via hyper-threading. The CPU includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, FMA, and AES. Memory capacity is set to 16.0 GB, delivering 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage architectures, and provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements place the compute and memory subsystem mostly in entry-level ranges relative to contemporary hardware. In synthetic evaluations, the processor scored 1108.19 in single-core and 5884.21 in multi-core stress-ng tests, ranking in the lower 25%. Geekbench results reflect a single-core score of 927.0 (bottom 10%) and a multi-core score of 3491.0 (bottom 25%), with compiling Clang reaching 5624.0. PassMark testing produced an overall CPU score of 7009.7 and an extended instructions score of 6058.53, both falling within the middle 50%, whereas the encryption score (2725.45) and memory score (1522.99) sat in the lower 25%. Uncached large-block memory read (40.86 GB/sec) and write (35.89 GB/sec) demonstrated median bandwidth performance.

Application and pipeline benchmarks align with these compute constraints. In compression benchmarks, single-threaded gzip registered 19.01 GB/sec (bottom 10%), while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 29.0 GB/sec (bottom 25%). Web and transactional tests reported static web serving throughput at 4.43 GB/sec, database operations at 2204.75, and Redis SET throughput at 5.68 million operations per second. For lightweight AI workloads, small 135M LLM models performed adequately at 466.0 tokens/sec prompt processing and 102.87 tokens/sec generation, but throughput dropped sharply on medium 7B models down to 10.1 tokens/sec prompt processing and 5.17 tokens/sec generation.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation and moderate compute envelope, the ecs.sn1ne.2xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for predictable background compute that does not require massive scale or modern single-core execution speed. Primary tradeoffs involve the absence of local NVMe storage, limited baseline networking, and generational CPU constraints. It is best applied to standard utility processing, modest web application servers, internal continuous integration builds, and small-footprint batch data transformations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized server powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor with 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs. Configured with a 1:2 compute-to-RAM ratio, it provides 16.0 GB of system memory, 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero bundled local storage, and no GPU accelerators. Synthetic and operational benchmarks indicate steady, mid-to-lower tier performance, earning 7009.7 on the PassMark CPU test and 3491.0 on multi-core Geekbench. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth sustains 40.86 GB/sec read and 35.89 GB/sec write. In application tests, it handles 5.68 million Redis SET operations per second and 4.43 GB/sec in static web serving. Lacking integrated NVMe drives and top-tier clock speeds, this instance represents a predictable, cost-aligned platform for distributed application layers, small background batch workloads, lightweight ETL, and internal build runners.
